scope: Published Proa documentation and named first-party or external integrations. Individual findings retain their review dates; capabilities are not inferred from benchmark rank.

ssr.note: Typed Rust templates render HTML on the server.

streaming.note: The streaming substrate supports in-order and out-of-order delivery through framework response adapters.

suspense.note: Suspense holds async children and fallback UI, with priority and timeout options.

client.note: RSJS islands activate immediately or through visible, idle, interaction, and media strategies.
client.label: RSJS islands

ssg.note: The reviewed deployment workflow produces a Rust server and public assets; a route-to-static-HTML export command is not established.

csr.note: RSJS activates server-authored islands and updates DOM; a standalone client-rendered application root is not established.

serverOnly.note: Ordinary Rust components stay on the server; only analyzed RSJS graphs become browser JavaScript. This is not the React RSC protocol.
serverOnly.label: Rust / RSJS boundary

partialRendering.note: Suspense streams request-time HTML; a prebuilt static shell with dynamic request holes is not established.

routing.note: The framework's route/page layer integrates request handling with Axum.
routing.label: Framework / Axum

layouts.note: Role-marked layouts nest around a selected Page. The handler composes them explicitly rather than using filesystem layout discovery.

dynamicRoutes.note: The Axum integration reads route parameters through the request context.
dynamicRoutes.label: Axum integration

parallelRoutes.note: The reviewed router/layout API does not establish independently navigable named route slots.

interceptedRoutes.note: The reviewed routing guide does not establish intercepted-modal/direct-entry route semantics.

prefetch.note: The documented optional Turbo integration prefetches eligible links on hover and supports explicit preloads. Plain rel=prefetch is a browser hint, not a Proa scheduler; Turbo must be installed separately.
prefetch.label: Turbo Drive

softNavigation.note: The documented Turbo Drive integration enhances ordinary server-rendered anchors with HTML swaps and browser history. Turbo is installed separately; normal document navigation remains the baseline.
softNavigation.label: Turbo Drive integration

viewTransitions.note: Turbo Drive can start browser View Transitions when both documents opt in with the view-transition meta tag. CSS controls the animation; unsupported browsers continue ordinary Turbo navigation. Apps must honor reduced-motion preferences.
viewTransitions.label: Turbo Drive

redirects.note: Framework handlers use Axum redirects and explicit response status; this source does not establish a rewrite configuration API.
redirects.label: Redirects via Axum

serverData.note: Keyed loaders share typed asynchronous results and feed streamed components.

clientData.note: RSJS queries seed from server data, expose fetch state, and support invalidating mutations against explicit URLs.

requestDedupe.note: Request-scoped keyed resolution deduplicates equivalent loads; cross-request policy is separate.

persistentCache.note: StandardDataLoader is an explicit process-local keyed cache with TTL, invalidate and clear. Share that loader across requests to reuse entries. Cross-instance storage and coordination require application-owned Redis/database/upstream integration; request-scoped DataResolver alone does not persist values.
persistentCache.label: StandardDataLoader / process local

invalidation.note: StandardDataLoader exposes key invalidation and clear; RSJS queries support explicit refresh/invalidation. Cache Trace records render dependencies for the application to consume. Recording a tag does not automatically purge a CDN or invalidate cached HTML.
invalidation.label: Explicit keys; app-owned CDN purge

isr.note: PageCache configures stale-while-revalidate/CDN behavior. There is no in-process page cache; without a CDN the page still renders.
isr.label: CDN-dependent

apiRoutes.note: Route::endpoint registers Axum handlers for JSON, forms, raw bodies, and webhooks.
apiRoutes.label: Axum integration

httpErrors.note: Axum handlers and managed Page/layout head hooks can set error statuses before the response is published. Managed status mutations report failure after headers are committed. Framework render/encoding failures have documented 500 responses when a replacement response is still possible; a late streaming error cannot replace the status already sent. A custom “not found” page must explicitly select 404.
httpErrors.label: Pre-commit status / Axum

actions.note: RSJS query/mutation helpers call explicit server URLs. The reviewed form guide uses an authored Axum POST handler, rather than a generated server-function RPC.
actions.label: Explicit endpoints

forms.note: Native forms submit to explicit Axum handlers; Wellformed validates inputs. Typed client actions are not generated server RPC.
forms.label: Forms + Wellformed

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Native forms submit to explicit Axum handlers; Wellformed validates inputs. Typed client actions are not generated server RPC.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Axum handlers/layers compose around endpoints; framework security layers apply to registered endpoints.
middleware.label: Axum layers

cookies.note: ResponseContext stages Set-Cookie values through append_set_cookie before headers are committed. Request parsing and session/identity policy remain host/application-owned.
cookies.label: Host HTTP integration

cssModules.note: The reviewed linked asset pipeline does not establish CSS Modules selector/class-map compilation.

scopedCss.note: ClassList and authored styles do not establish automatic component-local CSS selector rewriting.

tailwind.note: The official guide configures external Tailwind tooling for Rust-authored classes; it is not a required styling runtime.
tailwind.label: Tailwind tooling recipe

cssInJs.note: The reviewed client/asset pipeline does not establish a CSS-in-JS compiler and SSR style registry.

images.note: No image transformation pipeline is provided. The app prepares variants and authors srcset/sizes itself.
images.label: Manual variants

fonts.note: proa_fonts vendors self-hosted fonts, hashes assets, emits preload CSS, and provides metric-matched fallbacks.
fonts.label: proa_fonts

scripts.note: proa_third_party supports consent-aware analytics and deferred scripts; browser execution still requires CSP authorization.
scripts.label: proa_third_party

assetPipeline.note: proa_fonts emits content-hashed font files, but the documented static-file setup does not provide a general image/CSS fingerprinting pipeline. Applications supply the static router, build tooling, URL references, and cache headers. Serving image.svg alone does not automatically give it a new URL when its contents change.
assetPipeline.label: Fonts; app-owned pipeline

staticAssets.note: FrameworkBuilder mounts an application-supplied static router; disk/embedded service and cache headers are explicit.
staticAssets.label: Static router

metadata.note: Managed head builders produce structured title, canonical, social, and named metadata at one head outlet.
metadata.label: Explicit, composable API

assessment.label: Explicit, composable API
assessment.summary: Structured metadata with field-level inheritance and clear operations; setup and document ordering are explicit.
strengths: Shared request loaders can feed both render_head and the page body.
Layout defaults, field patches, explicit clears, and absolute titles are documented.
tradeoffs: Requires managed-head setup, role-marked components, and a head outlet; direct body rendering skips the metadata hook.
Metadata seals before the selected page body; it cannot be treated as unrestricted late head mutation.

dynamicMetadata.note: Async render_head can use the same keyed loader as the body; metadata seals before the selected Page body starts.

metadataInheritance.note: Layout hooks supply defaults; child hooks change only the fields they write. Handlers must compose role-marked components.

metadataOverrides.note: Children can patch or clear inherited fields. Image arrays replace the inherited list; images([]) removes it.
metadataOverrides.label: Field patches / clears

titleTemplates.note: title_template composes inherited titles; absolute_title bypasses it and clear_title_template resets it.

socialImages.note: Optional proa_og generates images using WPE WebKit on Linux and requires native libraries; metadata itself only emits image URLs.
socialImages.label: proa_og / Linux

sitemaps.note: Typed and asynchronous generators support individual sitemap documents and a multi-sitemap index.

robots.note: Structured generators support user-agent groups, sitemap links, and asynchronous generation.

markdown.note: md! / md_sync! render typed Markdown output. This is not itself a filesystem Markdown-to-HTML content pipeline.
markdown.label: Typed Markdown output

collections.note: Proa Docs compiles frontmatter schemas, file-routed Markdown, search/navigation data, and a static Rust page registry. It is documentation-content tooling.
collections.label: Proa Docs

draftMode.note: Application cache hints/bypass can implement previews, but a dedicated authenticated editorial draft API is not established.

translations.note: The reviewed published rendering API does not establish locale message catalogs, interpolation keys, and pluralization.

localeRouting.note: Application routes can carry a locale segment; automatic language negotiation/locale URL policy is not established.

localeFormatting.note: The reviewed published renderer does not establish locale-aware date/number formatter APIs.

auth.note: Axum extractors/middleware can authenticate requests. Identity storage, login, and session policy require application/library code.
auth.label: Host authentication hooks

csp.note: Configured CSP can assign a fresh per-response nonce to generated scripts; CSP and HSTS are opt-in.

cspNonce.note: Opt-in strict CSP generates a fresh 128-bit nonce per response and applies it to framework bootstraps, import maps and streaming scripts. Authored scripts must use the request nonce too; nonce-bearing HTML must not be reused as a shared cached response.
cspNonce.label: Strict CSP / streaming nonces

csrf.note: Default outer hardening rejects unsafe browser cross-origin writes unless trusted, covering pages and endpoints. This is origin-based protection, not a CSRF-token service; same-origin XSS and stolen sessions require other defenses.
csrf.label: Origin checks; no tokens

environment.note: The application defines and validates runtime environment configuration. Only explicitly selected values should enter browser props.
environment.label: Application-owned config

assessment.summary: Only analyzed RSJS client graphs become JavaScript; runtime configuration and serialization policy remain explicit application work.
strengths: The documented server-only boundary keeps ordinary server implementation out of browser modules.
tradeoffs: The application must validate environment configuration and select safe browser props/query seeds. A typed value can still contain a secret.

types.note: Rust type checking and template macros validate typed server templates at compile time.

hmr.note: proa dev watches files and rebuilds assets/server. This source does not promise React-style state-preserving hot updates.
hmr.label: Watch / rebuild

cli.note: proa dev and proa build coordinate project assets and compilation through proa.config.json.

bundleAnalysis.note: Linked asset/descriptor diagnostics help inspect generated client artifacts; a module-size visualization is not established.
bundleAnalysis.label: Linked artifact diagnostics

unitTests.note: Rust library tests use cargo test; linked RSJS integration targets use proa test.
unitTests.label: Rust / proa test

e2eTests.note: The guide recommends browser automation for behavior/accessibility workflows, but does not supply a dedicated browser runner.
e2eTests.label: Application browser tests

observability.note: Cache Trace exposes render/cache dependency diagnostics, and host tracing supplies production logging. Exporters and monitoring dashboards remain application-owned; those are not required by this instrumentation category.
observability.label: Cache traces / host logging

errorHandling.note: The published guide documents HTTP errors, fallback responses, and logging. A documented general component recovery-boundary contract is not established here.
errorHandling.label: HTTP fallback handling

serverHosting.note: Deploy a release binary plus public assets on your own server.

subpathProxy.note: Proa has built-in base-path support through FrameworkBuilder::with_base_path. Configure the public prefix at startup for a proxy that strips it before forwarding. BasePath-aware URL helpers and linked RSJS asset serving keep generated links, runtime imports and island loads aligned. Incoming routes remain unprefixed; authored links, forms, images and redirects use cx.url or app_url. The prefix is explicit, not inferred from forwarded headers.
subpathProxy.label: Built-in BasePath support

staticHosting.note: Compiled static article fragments still run inside the Rust request handler. A complete static-site export workflow is not established.

containers.note: The documented Docker build packages the Rust binary and required assets for a production runtime.

edgeHosting.note: Cloudflare can cache/proxy origin responses, but the reviewed deployment guide does not establish running Proa SSR inside Workers.

orm.note: The database guide integrates external SQLx, Diesel and Toasty behind DataLoader. Proa ships no database driver or ORM; these libraries supply queries and models, with their own installation and configuration.
orm.label: SQLx / Diesel / Toasty

migrations.note: proa add database scaffolds SQLx/SQLite and proa db runs the external library’s migrations. This is an integrated CLI workflow for SQLx, not a Proa-owned schema/migration engine.
migrations.label: SQLx via Proa CLI

transactions.note: The documented SQLx data-layer integration can use SQLx transactions, with commit, rollback and rollback-on-drop supplied by that external library. Proa provides no transaction manager; database lifetime, loader boundaries and retry policy remain application-owned.
transactions.label: SQLx data-layer integration

jobs.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned background jobs API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

mail.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned email API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

uploads.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned file uploads & storage API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

realtime.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned real-time delivery API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

xssEscaping.note: Dynamic template values are encoded for their HTML context, including separate URL policy. UnsafeRaw bypasses output protection; it does not sanitize user-authored rich HTML.

htmlSanitization.note: The reviewed escaping API encodes output and offers UnsafeRaw, but does not establish a maintained allowlist-based sanitizer. UnsafeRaw is a trust bypass, not a way to clean untrusted rich HTML.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: The documented native HTML form submits to an explicit Axum handler that validates and writes data. This path works without client handlers; RSJS actions enhance controls but are not generated server RPC or automatic form rollback.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Native forms / Axum

optimisticUi.note: The reviewed query/mutation guide establishes pending/error state and invalidation, but not an optimistic overlay with reconciliation/rollback. An authored signal update alone is not evidence of that contract.

requestCancellation.note: RSJS query observers move to the cache entry for a new structural key, so an old entry’s request stays with that entry. Full page-generation teardown cancels scheduled work and in-flight queries and invalidates old handles. This does not mean every key change aborts the previous shared request or undoes a server mutation.
requestCancellation.label: Query ownership / generation teardown

typedLinks.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific typed links & parameters contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

stateRestoration.note: Requires the documented optional Turbo integration, not Proa's plain document navigation. Turbo Drive caches page snapshots for restoration visits and supports data-turbo-permanent elements. Snapshots are DOM state, not a guarantee to serialize arbitrary JavaScript state; applications must implement lifecycle cleanup.
stateRestoration.label: Turbo snapshots

scrollRestoration.note: Requires the documented optional Turbo integration, not Proa's plain document navigation. Turbo restoration visits restore the recorded page scroll position. This establishes window/document restoration, not arbitrary nested scrollport state.
scrollRestoration.label: Turbo Drive

navigationBlocking.note: Requires the documented optional Turbo integration, not Proa's plain document navigation. turbo:before-visit can cancel an application visit. This does not intercept every browser history restoration or tab close; beforeunload remains a separate browser mechanism.
navigationBlocking.label: Turbo visit events

navigationAccessibility.note: Requires the documented optional Turbo integration, not Proa's plain document navigation. Turbo documents aria-busy during requests, focus of autofocus elements and updating the document title. It does not promise the same route-announcement/live-region contract as SvelteKit.
navigationAccessibility.label: Turbo focus / busy state

a11yChecks.note: The HTML compiler checks statically visible accessibility requirements, including required attributes and supported ARIA contracts. Runtime focus/contrast and cross-component context still need integration checks; these diagnostics do not certify accessibility.
a11yChecks.label: Compile-time checks

lazyActivation.note: RSJS final owners activate immediately or on visible, idle, interaction or media triggers. Server HTML is present first; runtime planning decides owner assets and query wiring. A delayed strategy is not a claim of zero browser runtime.
lazyActivation.label: RSJS strategies

codeSplitting.note: RSJS emits linked per-owner island modules, and a page runtime plan selects modules for rendered owners. Shared runtime dependencies may be needed; this differs from route-level SPA chunking.
codeSplitting.label: RSJS owner modules

offline.note: The linked deployment API review does not establish the specific offline integration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scheduling.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific scheduled tasks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

notifications.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific multi-channel notifications contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchIndex.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific search indexing contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

fieldEncryption.note: The linked database API review does not establish the specific encrypted model fields contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

httpTests.note: The linked testing API review does not establish the specific http integration tests contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.
